textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · Filling and Lifting · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: The amount a vessel can hold is called its capacity. We can compare two glasses by pouring from one to the other.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The amount a vessel can hold is called its capacity. We can compare two glasses by pouring from one to the other. If a small glass is filled and poured into a big glass, the big glass does not fill up. So it holds more.
beats.speakEn: The amount a vessel can hold is called its capacity. We can compare two glasses by pouring from one to the other. If a small glass is filled and poured into a big glass, the big glass does not fill up. So it holds more.

beats.en: A litre is a unit that we use to measure how much liquid a vessel holds. Milk is often measured in litres. A measuring cup is used to give 1 litre of milk, so everybody gets the same amount.
beats.speakEn: A litre is a unit that we use to measure how much liquid a vessel holds. Milk is often measured in litres. A measuring cup is used to give 1 litre of milk, so everybody gets the same amount.

type: Key Concept: The amount a vessel can hold is called its capacity.
Rule: A litre is a unit that we use to measure how much liquid a vessel holds.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · Filling and Lifting · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Some things are heavier and some are lighter. A pan balance helps to see which is heavier, because the heavier object makes its pan go down.

beats.en: Some things are heavier and some are lighter. A pan balance helps to see which is heavier, because the heavier object makes its pan go down. We can weigh a pencil by balancing it with coins or erasers.
beats.speakEn: Some things are heavier and some are lighter. A pan balance helps to see which is heavier, because the heavier object makes its pan go down. We can weigh a pencil by balancing it with coins or erasers.

beats.en: Three balls look the same, but one is heavier. We place one ball on each pan, and keep the third aside. If the pans balance, the ball left aside is the heavy one. If one pan goes down, that pan holds the heavy ball.
beats.speakEn: Three balls look the same, but one is heavier. We place one ball on each pan, and keep the third aside. If the pans balance, the ball left aside is the heavy one. If one pan goes down, that pan holds the heavy ball.
